summary: STEM closed-loop algorithm selection, model convergence criteria, automated hyperparameter bounds, and fallback triggers.

sections.content:
AI-ConneX

ML STUDIO — S.T.E.M.

Split • Train • Evaluate Metrics • Judge • Score • DeliverOne-Loop Multi-DAG / Multi-Family Architecture

ML Studio is the model-building execution environment of AI-ConneX. It is entered either from a new user intent through Jane or from Data Studio after industrial data has been prepared and feature-engineered. In both paths Jane discusses and confirms the model-building plan before expensive execution.

When Data Studio supplies the input, ML Studio receives a standard STEM recipe template covering Split, Train and Evaluate Metrics. When ML Studio is invoked independently as a microservice, Jane first runs a clean-validator. If the data is not sufficiently prepared, Jane explains the missing steps and recommends Data Studio. If it is clean, ML Studio creates a new manifest and invokes the DAG Assigner and Recipe Orchestrator once to obtain candidate DAG IDs, Family IDs and STEM recipes.

The core is a one-loop experiment: for every suggested DAG and Family ID, the system performs the approved split, trains all suggested models, evaluates all models with declared metrics, and then uses Judge and Scorer Agents to select the best acceptable model with reasons.

USER | vJANE | | +--> new intent --------------------+ |                                     | +--> Data Studio ---------------------+                                       v                                MODEL PLAN                                       |                         +-------------+-------------+                         |                           |                  STEM ONE-LOOP               NO ACCEPTABLE                         |                     MODEL PATH             DAG x FAMILY x MODEL                         |                Split -> Train -> Evaluate                         |                  Judge + Scorer                         |                         v                 Best Model + Reasons

ML Studio is not a replacement for Data Studio. Data Studio makes industrial data understandable and model-ready; ML Studio performs controlled model experimentation, comparison and selection.

The validator is a safety boundary, not a second Data Studio. It checks whether the dataset is sufficiently ready for the declared model task.

tables:
| Check | Validation |
| --- | --- |
| Schema | Required fields and types exist |
| Missingness | Within configured policy |
| Duplicates | Prediction unit is not ambiguously duplicated |
| Target | Exists and is trainable |
| Leakage | Known target/future leakage patterns absent |
| Time ordering | Valid for temporal tasks |
| Units | Known/compatible where required |
| Null handling | No unexpected unresolved nulls |
| Outlier policy | Declared or accepted |
| Feature provenance | Lineage available |
| Sample sufficiency | Enough observations/classes |
| Manifest integrity | Hashes and identity valid |

ML Studio should not silently repair major data-quality problems and then train. The user is told what is missing and why Data Studio is recommended.

ML_MANIFEST|+-- manifest_uid+-- parent_manifest_uid (optional)+-- dataset_uid+-- intent_uid+-- clean_validation_uid+-- DAG candidates+-- Family IDs+-- STEM recipe references+-- feature lineage+-- split/evaluation policy+-- compliance status+-- hashes

If the dataset came from Data Studio, the existing manifest lineage is retained. If it entered ML Studio independently, the new manifest establishes a new lineage root or parent relationship.

sections.section_path: DOC-SPEC-010 > 10. Why DAG + Recipe Orchestrator Runs Once
sections.content:
Obtains the candidate execution plan.

Obtains Family IDs and STEM recipe references.

Freezes the experiment space.

Prevents plan regeneration during model comparison.

Improves reproducibility and auditability.

Reduces unnecessary agent/tool calls.

A material change in objective, data, split policy or feature definition creates a new plan/version rather than mutating the active experiment.
Judge and Scorer are downstream decision agents; they do not replace STEM evaluation.
tables:
| Letter | Meaning | Responsibility |
| --- | --- | --- |
| S | Split | Create approved train/validation/test or temporal/group-aware partitions |
| T | Train | Train every approved model candidate |
| E | Evaluate | Evaluate every trained model on held-out data |
| M | Metrics | Normalize, store and compare declared evaluation metrics |

for DAG in suggested_DAGs:    for FAMILY in suggested_Families:        SPLIT = stem.split(DATA, DAG, FAMILY)        for MODEL in FAMILY.suggested_models:            MODEL_ARTIFACT = stem.train(MODEL, SPLIT.train)            METRICS = stem.evaluate(MODEL_ARTIFACT,                                    SPLIT.validation,                                    SPLIT.test)            store(DAG, FAMILY, MODEL, METRICS)Judge(all_results)Scorer(all_results)Select(best_acceptable)

Implementation may execute candidates in parallel, but logically all candidates belong to one versioned experiment graph.
Different DAGs represent alternative valid transformations, dependencies, aggregation paths or temporal structures. Each candidate must remain separately identifiable.

| DAG-A | Raw sensor → window aggregation → target |
| DAG-B | Sensor + environmental alignment → features → target |
| DAG-C | Entity aggregation → contextual features → target |

Judge is the reasoned suitability layer. It compares validated candidates against the user objective and industrial constraints.

Checks metric objective.

Checks hard constraints.

Checks generalization evidence.

Checks stability.

Checks leakage/validation status.

Checks complexity and resource cost.

Checks interpretability requirements.

Explains trade-offs.

Produces a shortlist or rejection.

Scorer applies a versioned quantitative selection policy. It must not change weights after seeing results.

score =    w1 * primary_metric_score  + w2 * secondary_metric_score  + w3 * stability_score  + w4 * resource_score  + w5 * interpretability_score  - penalties

Weights, metric direction and penalty rules are configuration and are included in the experiment record.

tables:
| Judge | Scorer |
| --- | --- |
| Qualitative comparative reasoning | Quantitative ranking |
| Explains suitability | Applies declared scoring policy |
| Finds trade-offs/disqualifiers | Produces normalized score |
| References evidence | References metric results |

sections.section_path: DOC-SPEC-010 > 38. Key R&D Failures and Mitigations
tables:
| Failure | Risk | AI-ConneX solution |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Train only one model | Biased selection | Train all approved candidates |
| Choose before evaluation | Confirmation bias | Evaluate before Judge |
| Regenerate DAG during trials | Unstable comparison | Freeze bootstrap plan |
| Assume incoming data is clean | Hidden leakage/errors | Clean-validator |
| Choose metric after seeing result | Metric gaming | Predeclare metric policy |
| Judge only by highest metric | Industrial constraints ignored | Judge + Scorer |
| Agent invents executable models | Unsafe execution | Controlled registry |
| Different split policies | Invalid comparison | Versioned split contract |
| Force a winner | Unsafe deployment | NO_ACCEPTABLE_MODEL state |
| No lineage | Untraceable result | Manifest + DAG + Family IDs |
| Agent changes data | Reproducibility risk | Proposal/validation separation |

A representative POC should use multiple DAGs, multiple Family IDs and multiple models so the One-Loop principle is demonstrable rather than theoretical.

Every approved candidate receives an evaluation record.

Every result contains DAG ID, Family ID and split ID.

No test-set fitting.

Metrics frozen before evaluation.

Judge references result IDs.

Scorer is reproducible from its policy.

Rejected models have machine-readable reasons.

Selected artifact has a cryptographic hash.

Lineage connects model → feature → dataset → intent.

Does multi-DAG/multi-Family evaluation improve model selection?

Does Judge + Scorer improve transparency?

Does clean validation reduce training failures?

Does freezing the bootstrap plan improve reproducibility?

How much industrial model-selection effort is reduced?

Does explicit rejection improve production safety?

H1: Multi-candidate STEM evaluation reduces selection of a suboptimal feasible model.

H2: Versioned split and metric policies improve reproducibility.

H3: Judge/Scorer separation improves explanation quality.

H4: Clean validation reduces downstream failures.

H5: Explicit lineage improves auditability.

| Training failure rate | Failed / attempted runs |
| Reproducibility | Repeated runs satisfying declared equivalence |
| Judge agreement | Human/agent agreement on suitability |
| Explanation completeness | Required rationale fields present |
| Selection latency | Plan approval to final selection |

Industrial users generally need a defensible answer to: What was trained, why was it trained, how was it evaluated, what alternatives were considered, why was this model selected, and can the decision be traced to the source data?

Jane converts business intent into a model plan.

Clean-validator prevents unsafe shortcuts.

DAG/Family IDs make alternatives explicit.

One-loop STEM makes comparison systematic.

Judge explains suitability.

Scorer applies declared policy.

Manifest and lineage make the result auditable.

ML Studio can explicitly return no acceptable model.

INTENT  | JANE  |MODEL PLAN  |  +---------------------------+  |                           |DATA STUDIO PATH        ML MICROSERVICE PATH  |                           |prepared + manifest      clean-validator  |                     /               |                   FAIL             PASS  |                    |                |  |               Data Studio       new manifest  |                                     |  +----------------+--------------------+                   |          DAG + RECIPE BOOTSTRAP ONCE                   |          FREEZE EXPERIMENT PLAN                   |       DAG × FAMILY × MODEL SPACE                   |        SPLIT → TRAIN → EVALUATE                   |                 METRICS                   |             JUDGE + SCORER                   |          BEST / NONE ACCEPTABLE                   |                 USER

The defining rule is: **do not guess the winner early**. Establish the plan, validate readiness, freeze the candidate space, evaluate all approved alternatives under a controlled contract, then let Judge and Scorer select—or explicitly reject all candidates.

AI-ConneX ML Studio is therefore a controlled model experimentation and selection system, not merely a training script. Its One-Loop S.T.E.M. process creates a comparable evidence set across multiple DAGs, Family IDs and models, while Jane maintains user intent, the clean-validator protects the boundary, and Judge + Scorer Agents turn validated results into an explainable selection.
